correctness.rationale: For periodic N>=3 upwind forward Euler v_i=(1-nu)u_i+nu u_{i-1} and consistent shared H(a,a)=U(a)=a^2/2, choose neighboring states (left,center,right)=(a,a,b) to force H(a,b)<=U(a), and (a,b,b) to force H(a,b)>=U(a)-(1-nu)(a-b)^2/2. At nu>1 these inequalities contradict each other for any a!=b. For 0<nu<=1 let J=U-H; the pointwise envelope is exactly 0<=J(a,b)<=(1-nu)(a-b)^2/2. Direct identity for any neighboring triple gives cell dissipation nu[(1-nu)(a-left)^2/2 +J(a,right)-J(left,a)]>=0, proving necessity and sufficiency without smoothness of H or bounded-state assumptions. Consistent quadratic polynomial H are exactly U(a)-k(a-b)^2 with 0<=k<=(1-nu)/2. Substituting the source half-cell bounds yields k<=1/2-nu, strictly narrower and void for nonconstant interfaces when nu>1/2. Independent rational counterexamples/witnesses check bounds; finite checks are not the universal proof.
